input: Carbon dioxide and hydrogen react over a copper-zinc oxide catalyst to give methanol. Two catalyst forms were compared on space-time yield, pressure drop and activity loss under one feed composition. Space-time yield is the mass of product per unit catalyst volume per hour (kg L-1 h-1). Test conditions were 280 °C and 40 bar, with a feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3. The structured catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.89 kg L-1 h-1, a pressure drop of 0.22 bar, and an activity loss of 8% after 100 h. The pellet catalyst gave a space-time yield of 0.49 kg L-1 h-1, a pressure drop of 1.31 bar, and an activity loss of 15% after 100 h. On the three measures together, the structured catalyst stands ahead at the conditions tested: yield 0.89 against 0.49 kg L-1 h-1, pressure drop 0.22 against 1.31 bar, activity loss 8% against 15% after 100 h. Each comparison is a comparison of the same two charges under the same test conditions (280 °C, 40 bar, feed ratio H2/CO2 = 3), so the differences belong to the catalyst form and not to the duty. The comparison rests on one feed composition, and no sulfur-bearing feed was tested, so the ranking is established for the tested feed only and carries no finding for a feed that bears sulfur. Yield and pressure drop are seldom reported for the same catalyst charge; both stand here for the charges tested, with the activity loss over the same 100 h, and that shared basis is the ground on which the comparison rests.
